questions.answer: As of 2026-07-01, a Northbay repair case may close if and only if identity is verified, no active hold exists, and either the routine packet is complete or all three exception conditions hold: minor repair scope, completed exception reconciliation, and register-defined exception authorization. The routine route needs no exception approval. These are the exhaustive routes. Unavailable evidence remains unknown rather than false, with three-valued evaluation determining whether the full condition is true, false, or unknown.

The exception route requires minor repair scope, complete exception reconciliation, and approval-register authorization, all necessary and together sufficient for that route. It substitutes for a complete routine packet, but does not waive identity verification or the requirement that there be no active hold.

Authorization is true exactly when the approval register records an unrevoked duty-supervisor approval with a matching case identifier. Explicit register rejection or revocation makes authorization false; unavailable required register evidence makes it null, meaning unknown. A requester email, vendor signature, inferred job title, or technician acceptance is not this authorization. Missing evidence must not be guessed or treated as rejection.

No. On 2026-07-01 major repairs fail the exception's necessary minor-scope condition, regardless of supervisor approval. The signed June decision expands scope only from 2026-10-01, not publication. The 2025 manager-email policy expired and was replaced; Southbay's major-repair rule has no Northbay authority. A major repair may still use the routine route if the packet, identity, and no-active-hold requirements are met.

Neither removes these conditions. The June memorandum is an unsigned, unapproved draft with no effective date; its proposals do not enact a change. The vendor recommendation is a supplier workflow preference with no authority to amend board rules, and payment alone is insufficient. The effective signed Northbay policy and annex retain exception reconciliation and the governing no-active-hold requirement. Reconciliation is an exception-route requirement, not an additional routine-route requirement.
